The Deputy Governor of Adamawa State, Prof. Kaletapwa Farauta, has sat for the Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria (TRCN) Professional Qualifying Examination (PQE). Her participation comes ahead of the council’s plan to enforce compulsory professional certification for teachers nationwide. The Registrar and Chief Executive Officer of TRCN, Dr Ronke Soyombo, disclosed this on Tuesday in Abuja during an interaction with newsmen. She said the deputy governor sat for the examination on Friday. Soyombo described her participation as a demonstration that everyone involved in education, irrespective of position or status, must meet professional teaching requirements. “In Adamawa State, for the first time, we actually saw the Deputy Governor of Adamawa State coming to sit for our exam. “She sat for the exam on Friday, and that is to tell you that everybody who owns schools or is making efforts in education is coming to sit for the exam,” she said. She stressed that no teacher would be exempted from the requirement. Soyombo explained that professional certification would be obtained once in a teacher’s lifetime, while practising licences would be renewed every three years. She said licence renewal would depend on evidence of participation in Mandatory Continuous Professional Development (MCPD) programmes. The registrar expressed concern over examination malpractice, revealing that the council uncovered more than 47 suspected impersonators during its latest Professional Qualifying Examination in Taraba State. She said TRCN had strengthened examination security through candidates’ photographs, surveillance cameras and other technological measures. According to her, the council had also upgraded its examination platform to accommodate 5,000 candidates simultaneously, from its initial capacity of 120. Soyombo disclosed that online registration had increased examination participation from about 13,000 candidates when she assumed office in May 2025 to approximately 26,000 by November 2025. She added that the council currently had more than two million teachers on its online platform, although compliance with professional licensing requirements remained low. This, she said, had prompted the introduction of an accelerated professionalisation pathway. On fraudulent certification, Soyombo said TRCN discovered 250 fake certificates during a teacher recruitment exercise in Nasarawa State. She added that a suspect identified as Godfrey was in custody over alleged certificate forgery. The registrar said the council had introduced Quick Response (QR) codes on certificates to facilitate verification. She said TRCN was also collaborating with the West African Examinations Council (WAEC) and the National Examinations Council (NECO) to strengthen enforcement. Soyombo disclosed that the council was proposing a requirement for schools to have at least 75 per cent of their teachers professionally certified before registering candidates for NECO examinations. (NAN) Agency Report
